The study focuses on the numerical simulation of a buoyant plume, which is a subject of extensive study due to its complex behaviors and challenges for simulation.
The governing equations used to model the buoyant plume are the non-isothermal Navier-Stokes equations with the Boussinesq approximation.
The finite volume method is used to discretize the governing equations, and the Pressure Implicit with Splitting of Operators (PISO) algorithm is employed to solve the pressure-velocity coupling.
Solving the Poisson equation for pressure correction can consume up to 80% of the computational time required to simulate incompressible fluid flow.
The hybrid methodology combines a neural network-based pressure field prediction with the PISO algorithm to accelerate the pressure correction step.
The neural network is trained to map physics-based cell-level features to the temporal changes in the pressure field, rather than predicting the entire pressure field at once.
The study evaluates the performance of the hybrid approach using several state-of-the-art iterative solvers, including multigrid and conjugate gradient methods.
The reference case simulates a 2D buoyant air plume in a 1 m x 1 m rectangular enclosure, with a unique inlet at the bottom and two outlets on the vertical walls.
The CFD solver is configured with a uniform Cartesian grid comprising 256 cells per meter, first-order time integration, and first-order upwind scheme for the convective terms.
The study demonstrates an average improvement of 94% in the initial guess for solving the Poisson equation and a mean acceleration factor of 3 for the first pressure corrector step.
The hybrid methodology is designed to be versatile, scalable, accurate, robust, and data-efficient, addressing common challenges with pure machine learning approaches.
The paper suggests that further research is required to demonstrate the scalability of the methodology to more complex cases and to identify effective ways to combine CFD with machine learning.
The open-source CFD software OpenFOAM (v2312) is used to simulate the transient flows, and the buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam solver is employed in PISO mode.
The boundary conditions for the buoyant plume simulations include no-slip walls, fixed-value inlet, and pressure-based outlet conditions.
The simulations are conducted without turbulence modeling, and the linear systems are solved iteratively with a tolerance of 10^-7 on the normalized residuals.
